---
title: Google TPU (experimental)
description: Single-chip fine-tuning on Google Cloud TPUs with TorchTPU
---

::: {.callout-warning}
TPU support is experimental and has not yet been validated on TPU hardware. Please report
results, good or bad, on [issue #3521](https://github.com/axolotl-ai-cloud/axolotl/issues/3521).
:::

Axolotl runs on Google Cloud TPUs through [TorchTPU](https://github.com/google-pytorch/torch_tpu),
the native PyTorch backend that replaces the deprecated PyTorch/XLA (`torch_xla`). TorchTPU
registers a `tpu` device, so the Hugging Face Trainer runs on it without TPU-specific code.

## Requirements

- A TPU VM with a TorchTPU-supported chip: v5e, v5p, v6e (Trillium) or v7x (Ironwood).
- Python 3.12 or newer.

## Installation

TorchTPU needs the CPU build of PyTorch. Without the extra index, pip installs the CUDA build.

```bash
pip install "axolotl[tpu]" --extra-index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu
```

## Quick start

Training runs on a single chip, so launch one process:

```bash
axolotl train examples/tpu/qwen3-0.6b-lora.yml --launcher python
```

When `torch_tpu` is the active accelerator, Axolotl:

- trains on `tpu:0`, loading the model on the host first;
- enables bf16 (`bf16: auto` resolves to bf16, `fp16: true` is switched to bf16 with a warning);
- pads every batch to `sequence_len` and drops the last incomplete batch, so the input shape never changes;
- skips the automatic Triton LoRA kernels.

See `examples/tpu/` for complete LoRA and full fine-tuning configs.

## Supported

- Supervised fine-tuning (SFT) with LoRA or full fine-tuning
- bf16
- `attn_implementation: sdpa` or `eager`
- `activation_checkpointing: true`
- `axolotl preprocess`

## Not supported yet

Axolotl rejects these at config validation with an error that names the option.

| Feature | Reason |
|---|---|
| Multi-chip training (DDP, FSDP, DeepSpeed, TP/CP/EP) | accelerate does not yet set up the TorchTPU process group ([huggingface/accelerate#4532](https://github.com/huggingface/accelerate/pull/4532)) |
| QLoRA, 8-bit/4-bit loading, bitsandbytes optimizers | bitsandbytes needs CUDA |
| Flash attention, xformers | CUDA kernels; use `sdpa` |
| Sample packing, batch flattening | batch shapes change every step |
| RL trainers (`rl:`) | SFT only for now |
| `torch_compile` | not yet validated with TorchTPU's `tpu` compile backend |
| Liger, Cut Cross Entropy, `lora_*_kernel` | CUDA/Triton kernels |
| `activation_checkpointing.offload` | relies on CUDA streams |
| `tf32`, `gpu_memory_limit`, `max_memory` | GPU-only options |

## Known limitations

- **Resuming from a checkpoint does not restore the TPU RNG state.** The Hugging Face Trainer
  does not save it yet, so a resumed run is not bit-for-bit reproducible.
- **Memory usage is not reported** in Axolotl's memory logs or telemetry on TPU.

## Troubleshooting

**Training runs on CPU.** Check that `python -c "import torch; print(torch.accelerator.current_accelerator())"`
prints `tpu`. If it doesn't, `torch_tpu` is not installed in the active environment.

**`Multi-chip TPU training is not supported yet`.** Axolotl was started with more than one
process. Use `--launcher python`.

**Slow first steps.** Expect the first steps to be slower while TorchTPU warms up.
